page.layout: One page of text in a single column. Running head at top, with page number 575 at the upper right. Then italic question headings and paragraphs, a rule, a large division heading (titulus) with a Latin and black-letter German title, and further italic headings and paragraphs. No marginal notes, no footnotes, no catchword or signature.

main_text.head: Quid Animalium nomine proditum est?
main_text.p: ANimalium nomine, quae ratione carent, si qua lascivia, aut pavore, aut feritate pauperiem fecerint: Noxalis actio lege duodecim tabularum prodita est. Quae animalia si noxae dedantur, proficiunt reo ad liberationem. in princ. inst. eod.
main_text.head: Quid est pauperies?
main_text.p: Pauperies est damnum sine injuria facientis datum. Nec enim potest animal injuriam fecisse dici, quod sensu caret. in princ. verf. pauperies. inst. eod.
main_text.head: Quidnam ædilitio edicto prohibetur?
main_text.p: Sciendum est ædilitio edicto prohiberi nos canes, verrem, aprum, ursum, leonem ibi habere, quà vulgo iter fit.[?] §. cæterum. inst. eod.
main_text.head: QUIS EST DECIMUS Titulus?
De iis, per quos agere possumus. Von denen durch welche wir klagen vnd rechtlich handlen mögen.
Cujus nomine agere possumus?
main_text.p: ADmonendi sumus agere posse quemlibet hominem, aut suo nomine, aut alieno. Alieno, veluti procuratorio, tutorio, in princ. inst. eo.
main_text.head: Quomodo constituitur procurator?
main_text.p: Procurator (ein[?] [illegible, ~8 letters]) neque certis verbis, neque praesente semper adversario, imo plerunque eo ignorante constituitur: cuicunque enim permissum est rem tuam agere, aut defendere: is tuus procurator intelligitur. §. procurator. inst. eod.

page.notes: The Greek word in parentheses after "Procurator" is not legible at this scan resolution; it is marked illegible. The "ein" before it is doubtful. The Latin "ADmonendi" has a large initial A joined to the word. "homi-nem" breaks across lines with no printed hyphen visible; written whole. "fit" after "iter" is doubtful (the scan looks like "lit" or "fit"). The German subtitle is set in black letter and is marked with bl. The large initial V in "Von" is decorative and is written as V. The heading "QUIS EST DECIMUS Titulus?" is the division heading; "Titulus" is set in italic type in the original.
